observations.explanation: The AlfWorld setup compares a reflection run with a retry-only baseline by skipping reflection when the heuristic triggers, explicitly aiming to distinguish learning from probabilistic success over retries (PDF p. 5). The paper reports solving 97% of 134 environments with reflection, supporting the claim at that scope (PDF p. 5).
The paper reports that HotPotQA ReAct-only retries added no correct answers, while the reflection agent improved across consecutive trials and reached 54% cumulative accuracy (PDF pp. 6–7).

The paper says an agent needs a termination heuristic and binary reward model (PDF p. 7), but does not establish that termination must be task-specific or that these requirements in fact impede transfer. It presents more specific heuristics as an option and gives examples of broadly applicable binary rewards (PDF pp. 7, 10).

On WebShop, the paper reports only a 33%→35% gain for Reﬂexion and says the agent was not generating helpful, intuitive self-reflections (PDF p. 10). The authors characterize this benchmark attempt as inconclusive (PDF p. 10).
